title: What If You Stood on the Bay of Fundy Seafloor at Low Tide?
subject: Bay of Fundy

scenes.text: What if you stood on this seafloor at low tide? Six hours later, it's gone.
The Bay of Fundy has some of the biggest tides on Earth, with a range of over 16 meters.
That is roughly the height of a five-story building, rising and falling in just six hours.
About 160 billion tonnes of seawater flow in and out of the bay with each tide.
That's more than all the world's freshwater rivers carry over the same six hours.
Tidal currents can top 10 knots, and the tide shifts about an hour later every day.
